newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TURN THE SCREW ON INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TURN THE SCREW ON INDIA.

text.p: South Africa posted their highest test score against India as they turned the screw on the wilting tourists on the second day of the second test on Friday.

All-rounder Brian McMillan -- 13 not out overnight -- lead the way with an undefeated 89 as South Africa accelerated to 454 for seven at tea. It surpassed their previous highest test score in nine meetings -- 428 recorded in Calcutta in December.
Resuming at 280 for four, South Africa lost the wickets of Hansie Cronje (41) and Shaun Pollock (1) in the first 10 overs. But that was the end of India's success.

McMillan and Dave Richardson (39) set a seventh wicket partnership record of 83 against India -- bettering their own previous best of 37 -- before McMillan and Lance Klusener posted an eighth-wicket record.

The pair put on an unbroken 72 at a run a minute with Klusener beginning aggressively, striking Javagal Srinath for three successive fours and reaching a test best 45 in just 50 balls. In all South Africa put on 115 between lunch and tea.
At tea Srinath had figures of three for 115 from 37 overs; Anil Kumble nought for 107 from 44 overs and Venkatesh Prasad's 30 overs had cost 99 runs for three wickets.
